overall_summary: Deduplication and recency weighting show that space and planetary 'What If' scenarios (especially extreme environments, bizarre planetary weather, and hypothetical physics falls) are vastly outperforming standard psychology, history, or basic animal facts on a views-per-day basis. Videos published within the last 7 to 10 days (e.g., A9Qa-RmuOr0, IYuce8vaU3Y, 8KEl0_pJ_68, 6pwazIPnOHw) maintain high velocity, strong like-to-view ratios, and active engagement compared to older catalog items.

winning_patterns.pattern: Hypothetical Planetary 'What If' / Extreme Environment Scenarios
winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (8KEl0_pJ_68) generate over 1,000 views rapidly with high like-to-view ratios.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on high-stakes hypothetical space scenarios involving bizarre or extreme planetary surfaces.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles featuring bizarre physics or extreme weather on real exoplanets (e.g., Venus day vs year, TrES-2b coal-dark planet) secure robust initial velocity and sustained engagement.
winning_patterns.action: Continue producing short-form concepts focused on paradoxical or counter-intuitive celestial mechanics.

weak_patterns.evidence: Topics like fake memories, song loops, and general brain facts (e.g., ef3ND4qiRHc, 5AN7LUgqarc, mGEgENcGcNE) stagnate in the double-digits with minimal velocity after initial drop.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standard psychological tricks unless reframed into high-stakes, high-mystery cinematic scenarios.

weak_patterns.evidence: Simple animal facts (e.g., octopuses having three hearts, jellyfish living forever) show slower growth and lower like-to-view ratios compared to deep-space hooks.
weak_patterns.action: Pivot animal content entirely toward cinematic animal survival or extreme prehistoric/evolutionary paradoxes if used.
